sql:
SELECT
  tm.title AS macro_title,
  tm.usage_count AS current_usage_count,
  COALESCE(ch.event_count, 0) AS logged_update_event_count,
  ch.sum_increment AS sum_of_logged_increments,
  ch.first_update_at AS first_logged_update_at,
  ch.last_update_at AS last_logged_update_at,
  tm.created_at AS macro_created_at
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, usage_count, created_at
  FROM macros
  ORDER BY usage_count DESC, id
  LIMIT 5
) tm
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    entity_id,
    COUNT(*) AS event_count,
    SUM((after_data->>'usage_count')::numeric - (before_data->>'usage_count')::numeric) AS sum_increment,
    MIN(occurred_at) AS first_update_at,
    MAX(occurred_at) AS last_update_at
  FROM change_history
  WHERE entity_table = 'macros'
    AND 'usage_count' = ANY(changed_columns)
  GROUP BY entity_id
) ch ON ch.entity_id = tm.id
ORDER BY tm.usage_count DESC, tm.id

Submitted. Summary of what the report does and the one deviation flagged to Ben:

- **Grain:** one row per macro, for the 5 macros with the highest current `usage_count`.
- Since the warehouse has no stored copy of last week's report output, I couldn't match by macro id against it — I used today's top 5 by `usage_count` as the closest available proxy and flagged this in the note so Ben can confirm it's the same set, or supply the prior report's macro ids if not.
- For each macro: `current_usage_count` straight from `macros`, plus `logged_update_event_count`, `sum_of_logged_increments` (sum of `after_data.usage_count - before_data.usage_count`), and first/last logged update timestamps from `change_history` (filtered to `entity_table = 'macros'` and `changed_columns` containing `'usage_count'`), alongside `macro_created_at` — exactly as requested, so the gap between logged increments and the actual counter will be visible per macro.
